chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abu Sa'id from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ja'far al-Ahwal from Uthman ibn Isa said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): What do you say about a man who is given the authority to perform Hajj on behalf of another, and he delegates it to someone else? He said: 'There is no harm in it.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And if a person performs Hajj on behalf of another and is prevented from completing part of the journey regarding the Hajj, he must return from what he took an amount equal to the expense of the remaining part of the journey in which the Hajj is performed, unless he guarantees the return to perform what is obligatory upon him. This is indicated by the fact that he hired him to traverse the entire distance and perform all the rituals; so if he traverses part of it and does not traverse the rest, it becomes obligatory upon him to return the wage of the remaining part of the journey, because that is the ruling of all rentals. If he guarantees fulfillment of it afterwards, he is not bound by that. Then the Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And if the deputy in Hajj dies, and his death is after entering the state of Ihram and entering the Haram, then the obligation of Hajj is lifted from him and that suffices for the one on whose behalf he performed Hajj. If he dies before entering Ihram and entering the Haram, then upon his heirs is the remainder of the expense of the journey that is still upon him, if he left something in their hands. We have clarified in what preceded that whoever performs Hajj for himself and dies after entering the Haram, the obligation of Hajj is lifted from him. If he dies before entering the Haram, then it does not suffice for him. And the ruling of whoever performs Hajj on behalf of another is the ruling of whoever performs Hajj for himself regarding the manner of the rituals.

key_terms.النَّائِبُ: The deputy or agent performing the ritual
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: The state of consecration for Hajj
key_terms.الْحَجَّةَ: The authority or mandate to perform Hajj on behalf of another
key_terms.الْمَنَاسِكِ: The rituals and rites of Hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings if a person hired to perform Hajj on behalf of another delegates the task or dies during the journey?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of a Hajj delegate (*na'ib*) sub-delegating the ritual, affirming it as valid unless otherwise specified. It establishes precise financial liabilities for the delegate based on the principle of *ijarah* (contract of service), requiring proportional refund if prevented from completing the journey, while distinguishing the legal consequences of death before versus after entering the *Haram*. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that Hajj on behalf of another is treated similarly to personal Hajj regarding the validity of rites and the discharge of obligation upon death within the sacred precincts.
